marks.gloss_en: the baraita permits consecration before Jubilee without the mishna's two-year exclusion
baraita: an ancestral field may be consecrated before or after Jubilee, though not during Jubilee itself
Rav and Shmuel read the mishna as advice against consecrating for redemption by annual deduction; consecration itself remains effective
less than two years before Jubilee one should not consecrate expecting redemption by annual deduction
a pre-Jubilee consecration does not simply return to its owner, so the sale a-fortiori cannot establish Shmuel's rule
Rav Yosef: the sale a-fortiori does not establish Shmuel's rule for consecration
Shmuel follows R. Shimon, under whom the priests enter without paying; Rav replies that even there the field does not return to its owner but is awarded from the divine table
Shmuel follows R. Shimon: the priests enter at Jubilee without paying, so the consecration leaves the treasury without redemption
mishna: one should not consecrate an ancestral field less than two years before Jubilee
Rav: a field consecrated during Jubilee is consecrated and redeemed for fifty sela per beit kor
